Internal `internal/json` package provides the abstraction. Custom field registry (`json.Registry`) enables type-safe deserialization of extension fields.
+`internal/json.FieldProbe` backs the sealed JWS/JWK building-block `Header` APIs.
+It indexes top-level members in owned input, preserves duplicates in document order
+(first-wins lookup), and validates nested values without allocating a value tree.
+`internal/json.HasField` is the allocation-light streaming presence check used by
+`jwk.Parse` to distinguish JWK from JWKS. Both use json/v2's pooled decoder and
+strict UTF-8/control-character validation; no third-party JSON parser is used.
+`VerifyCompactFast` enforces its minimal-shape gate and refusal sentinels on top
+of the probe. Invalid JSON string encodings (raw control characters, invalid
+UTF-8, lone surrogate escapes) fail on both `VerifyCompactFast` and `jws.Verify`.

- **AlgorithmsForKey()** — DEPRECATED. Do not use it, and do not add callers. It is the internal helper jwx uses to guess algorithms for a JWKS key with no `alg`, exported only because it always has been. The code now lives in `jws/internal/keyalg` (`keyalg.Candidates`), which everything in the tree calls directly. It works until the next major version and gets no fixes, and the way it picks algorithms must not change (the list still grows when an extension registers, since the tables are an input). Do NOT patch it. It is a one-line wrapper only because `keyalg` still picks the same way it did before deprecation; when that changes, copy the old code back into `AlgorithmsForKey` instead of letting the change through.

- Sub-package: `jws/internal/keyalg` — key-to-algorithm classification. Owns the process-global registration tables behind `RegisterAlgorithmForKeyType`/`RegisterAlgorithmForCurve` (as `RegisterForKeyType`/`RegisterForCurve`), plus `Candidates` (which algorithms a key could be used with), `KeyTypesFor` (reverse lookup), `ValidateEd25519KeyShape`, and the `ErrUnclassifiableKey` sentinel. Registers the builtin algorithms from its own `init()`.

- ML-DSA (go1.27): `mldsa.go` installs a `Signer`/`Verifier` pair per parameter set. Both accept a raw `crypto/mldsa` key or an AKP `jwk.Key`, and both reject a key whose parameter set disagrees with the algorithm. The signature primitives come from `lestrrat-go/dsig` v1.4.0, which owns the algorithm registration.

- ECDSA curve binding (opt-in): `WithStrictECDSA(bool)` is a `SignVerifyOption` that rejects a key whose curve disagrees with ES256/ES384/ES512 per RFC 7518 Section 3.4. OFF by default. `jws/internal/jwsbb.RequireECDSACurve` is reached through `signatureBuilder.Build`, `signStreaming`, `verifyContext.tryKey`, and `verifyStreaming`, each gated on its context's `strictECDSA` flag. JWKS algorithm inference is unchanged; strict verification checks each selected pair afterwards. Use `jwt.WithSignOption(jws.WithStrictECDSA(true))` for signing or `jwt.WithVerifyOption(jws.WithStrictECDSA(true))` for parsing. The latter routes JWT verification through `jws.Verify`, avoiding both compact fast paths. `jws/jwsbb` and `jws.VerifyCompactFast` remain permissive; use `jws.Verify` when strict verification is required.
